'''Ricardo Alberto Silveira de Carvalho''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Infante D. Henrique|OIH]] [[Order of Merit (Portugal)|ComM]]}} ({{IPA|pt|ʁiˈkaɾðu kɐɾˈvaʎu}}; born 18 May 1978) is a Portuguese [[association football|football]] coach and former player who is assistant head coach of the [[Portugal national football team|Portugal national team]]. He is widely regarded as one of the best [[centre-back]]s of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The 50 best defenders in football history ranked by fans |url=https://www.givemesport.com/football-fans-rank-the-50-greatest-defenders-in-football-history/|website=GiveMeSport |date=9 April 2020 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Remembering Greatness: Ricardo Carvalho|author=Daniel Feliciano|url=https://tapinsandtapouts.com/2021/06/04/remembering-greatness-ricardo-carvalho/|publisher=Tap Ins & Tap Outs|date=4 June 2021|access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Top quotes on Ricardo Carvalho|author=Hitesh Darji|url=https://www.footiecentral.com/20220606/top-quotes-on-ricardo-carvalho/|publisher=Footie Central|date=6 June 2022|access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> 

Carvalho began his career at [[FC Porto|Porto]], where he had loan spells at [[Leça F.C.|Leça]], [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]] and [[F.C. Alverca|Alverca]], before winning domestic and European trophies under [[José Mourinho]]'s management. In July 2004, Carvalho transferred to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] for a fee of just under €30&nbsp;million. With the Blues, he won two [[Premier League]] titles in a row and one [[Football League Cup|League Cup]], in his first two seasons. In 2008, he was voted the team's Players' Player of the Year. Two years later, he helped Chelsea win the [[2009–10 Premier League|league]] and [[2010 FA Cup Final|FA Cup]], the first [[Double (association football)|Double]] in the club's history. In August 2010, after six years with Chelsea, he transferred to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for a fee of £6.7&nbsp;million, winning two domestic honours under Mourinho's management before a free transfer to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in 2013.

In international football, Carvalho's national team career began on 11 October 2003 in a friendly match against [[Albania national football team|Albania]]. He represented Portugal in three [[UEFA European Championship]]s and two [[FIFA World Cup]]s, and was a member of the team that won [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. He was a regular in Portugal's lineup during [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]], when his country advanced all the way to the [[UEFA Euro 2004 Final|final]] before losing to [[Greece national football team|Greece]]. At the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]], he played in six matches for Portugal, who finished fourth after reaching the semi-finals.

==Club career==

===Porto (1997–2004)===
Ricardo Carvalho was brought to the [[FC Porto|Porto]] junior team in the 1996–97 season. In the oncoming season, Carvalho made his professional debut when he signed on loan for [[Leça F.C.|Leça]]. Between 1999 and 2001, he had loan spells at [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]] and [[F.C. Alverca|Alverca]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=14765 |title= FC Porto cede Ricardo Carvalho ao V. Setúbal |trans-title= FC Porto provides Ricardo Carvalho to V. Setúbal |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language= pt |date= 30 September 1999 |access-date= 11 January 2011 |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120324213550/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=14765 |archive-date= 24 March 2012 |df= dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=40688 |title= Ricardo Carvalho segunda-feira em Alverca |trans-title= Ricardo Carvalho will be on Monday in Alverca |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language= pt |date= 23 July 2000 |access-date= 11 January 2011 |archive-date= 24 March 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120324213612/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=40688 |url-status= dead }}</ref> He returned to Porto in the [[2001–02 Primeira Liga|2001–02 season]], being third choice behind [[Jorge Costa (footballer)|Jorge Costa]] and [[Jorge Andrade]], but he quickly won a place in the starting XI, forming a terrific partnership with Andrade in the centre of defence, which brought disappointment to [[Captain (association football)|captain]] Jorge Costa who,<ref>{{cite web | url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=102807 | title= Pinto da Costa: "Jorge Costa não é problema meu..." | trans-title= Pinto da Costa "Jorge Costa it's not my problem..." | publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] | language= pt | date= 26 October 2001 | access-date= 11 January 2011 | archive-date= 24 March 2012 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120324214037/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=102807 | url-status= dead }}</ref> in April 2002, joined [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on a five-month loan spell.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/charlton_athletic/1937739.stm | title = Charlton complete Costa move | date = 18 April 2002 | access-date =10 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> Carvalho made 25 appearances in the [[Primeira Liga|Portuguese league]] that season.<ref name="National_Team_P">{{NFT player|id=5287|name=Ricardo Carvalho|accessdate=12 October 2009}}</ref> In the following [[2002–03 Primeira Liga|season]], Jorge Costa returned to Porto and Jorge Andrade moved to [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] in Spain.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaJAndrade22072002.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205171120/http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaJAndrade22072002.pdf|archive-date=5 December 2010|title=Venda do passe do jogador Jorge Andrade|trans-title=Player Jorge Andrade's pass sold|publisher=[[FC Porto]]|language=pt|date=22 July 2002|access-date=4 October 2010}}</ref> With [[José Mourinho]] in charge, Carvalho started the campaign as the third option behind Costa and [[Pedro Emanuel]],<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=141719 | title= Ricardo Carvalho volta a ser titular |trans-title= Ricardo Carvalho returns to starting 11 |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] | language= pt | date= 9 November 2002 | access-date=11 January 2011 }}</ref> but later, his excellent form led him to a place in the first team,<ref>{{cite web | url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=156298 | title= Tempo de afirmação | trans-title= Statement time | publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] | language= pt | date= 3 April 2003 | access-date= 11 January 2011 | archive-date= 24 March 2012 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120324214111/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=156298 | url-status= dead }}</ref> appearing in the most important games of the season, including the [[2002–03 UEFA Cup#Semi-finals|UEFA cup semi-finals]] matches against [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] and the [[2003 UEFA Cup Final|UEFA Cup final]] where Porto beat [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] 3–2 in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]]. It was Carvalho's first international trophy. By his great season, he was named [[CNID Footballer of the Year#Portuguese League Footballer of the Year (2001–present)|Portuguese League Footballer of the Year]] and Porto Footballer of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=157748 |title= Mourinho e Costinha são Dragões de Ouro |trans-title= Mourinho and Costinha are Golden Dragons |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language= pt |date= 17 April 2003 |access-date= 11 January 2011 |archive-date= 24 March 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120324214123/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=157748 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

It was in the [[2003–04 Primeira Liga|2003–04 season]] that Carvalho made his name as a world-class footballer. His solid performances helped the club win the Portuguese league title for the second year in a row, and the most prestigious club trophy in European football, the [[UEFA Champions League]]. In this tournament, Carvalho played in all of Porto's matches, including the 3–0 win against [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the [[2004 UEFA Champions League Final|final]]. Subsequently, his great performances merited the [[UEFA Club Football Awards#Award categories|UEFA Club Best Defender of the Year]] award, voted into the [[UEFA Team of the Year]], and was named one of the 50 players shortlisted for the [[2004 Ballon d'Or]]), finishing ninth in the voting, being the only defender in top ten.<ref>{{Cite web| url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy04.html | title = European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 2004 | date = 14 December 2004 | access-date =24 November 2009 | work = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSS]] }}</ref> He was selected for the Portuguese [[UEFA Euro 2004]] [[UEFA Euro 2004 squads#Portugal|squad]], in which tournament he was also nominated for the [[UEFA Euro 2004#Awards|UEFA Euro Team of the Tournament]]. At the end of the season, Carvalho has been tracked by a host of top European clubs, including [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=201769 |title= Doidos por Ricardo |trans-title= Madness by Ricardo |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language= pt |date= 25 June 2004 |access-date= 13 January 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120406191532/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=201769 |archive-date= 6 April 2012 |url-status= dead |df= dmy-all }}</ref> Real Madrid offered [[Euro|€]]8.2 ([[Pound sterling|£]]7) million for Carvalho, but Porto warned the Spaniards they would not accept anything less than €23.5 (£20) million for the defender after the Spanish team made a much lower offer.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3904575.stm | title = Carvalho priced at £20m | date = 18 July 2004 | access-date =24 November 2009 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> Days later, English club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] offered €30 (£25.5) million for the centre back, which the Portuguese team accepted.<ref name="Chelsea sign Carvalho">{{Cite web| url = http://www.rediff.com/sports/2004/jul/28chelsea.htm | title = Chelsea sign defender Carvalho | date = 28 July 2004 | access-date =19 October 2009 | work = [[Rediff.com]] }}</ref><ref name="2003_04_report">{{Cite news| url = http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/RelatoriosContas/ParteI_ingles.pdf | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101205142220/http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/RelatoriosContas/ParteI_ingles.pdf | archive-date=5 December 2010 | title = Annual Report 2003•2004 (''page 21'') | date = 1 October 2004 | access-date =29 October 2009 | work = [[FC Porto]] }}</ref>

===Chelsea (2004–2010)===
At [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], Carvalho, who was considered one of the best centre-backs at Euro 2004, joined his former manager José Mourinho and former teammate [[Paulo Ferreira]]<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/3782871.stm | title = Chelsea to sign Ferreira | date = 23 June 2004 | access-date =20 September 2009 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/859229|title=Ricardo Carvalho completes the squad|date=27 July 2004|access-date=15 April 2014|work=Chelsea F.C.|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517143338/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/859229|archive-date=17 May 2014}}</ref> He signed for a fee of €30 million (£20 million at the time)<ref name="2003_04_report"/> and performed extremely well in his first season with Chelsea, helping them win the [[Premier League]] title, their first top-flight domestic title in 50 years, and the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]]. He scored his first goal for Chelsea in a 3–1 victory over [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].<ref>[http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/27945 Norwich City 1 v 3 Chelsea – Match Report] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20140415165815/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/27945 |date=15 April 2014 }}, [[Chelsea F.C.]] Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> His partnership with [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[John Terry]] in central defence was hailed as a major factor behind Chelsea's two Premier League titles in a row.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,14621_3593059,00.html| title= Ricardo Carvalho | date= 24 May 2008 | access-date=24 November 2009 | work = [[Sky Sports]] }}</ref>

[[File:Ricardo Carvalho tour.JPG|thumb|upright|170px|right|Ricardo Carvalho on tour with Chelsea in 2007.]]
The start of [[2005–06 Chelsea F.C. season|2005–06 season]] was not as smooth for him, as he was publicly lambasted by Mourinho after making comments about his selection policy. Carvalho said the Chelsea manager's decision to drop him for the first game of the season was "incomprehensible", but Mourinho responded, "Carvalho seems to have problems understanding things, maybe he should have an IQ test," and then left him out for next game, against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], and fined him a reported £85,000.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/4165022.stm | title= Mourinho angered by Carvalho rant | date= 19 August 2005 | access-date=14 May 2005 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/4166638.stm | title= Carvalho fined for Mourinho rant | date= 23 August 2005 | access-date=14 May 2005 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> He later returned to favour, though, and was a near-regular in the side from September. On 19 October 2005, he scored his first goal of the season in a 4–0 home win against [[Real Betis]] in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League#Group stage|UEFA Champions League group stage]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielbericht/champions-league-2005-2006-gruppe-g-chelsea-fc-real-betis/ | title= Chelsea FC vs Real Betis – Match Report | date= 19 October 2005 | access-date=14 May 2005 | work = Weltfussball.de }}</ref> Carvalho continued his scoring run in [[UEFA|Europe]] by netting his second goal of the season in Chelsea's 2–0 away victory over [[RSC Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] on 23 November.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielbericht/champions-league-2005-2006-gruppe-g-rsc-anderlecht-chelsea-fc/ | title= RSC Anderlecht vs Chelsea FC – Match Report | date= 23 November 2005 | access-date=14 May 2005 | work = Weltfussball.de }}</ref> In January, in a 1–1 Premier League draw against [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], Carvalho received the first [[Misconduct (football)|red card]] of his Chelsea career, after he received his second yellow for what the referee judged to be a tackle from behind on Charlton striker [[Darren Bent]].<ref>{{Cite news | url= http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/30725 | archive-url= https://archive.today/20140415165814/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/30725 | url-status= dead | archive-date= 15 April 2014 | title= Chelsea 1 v 1 Charlton – Match Report | date= 22 January 2006 | access-date= 15 April 2014 | publisher= [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref> Later, on 29 April 2006, he scored again a goal, his third of the season, in a 3–0 Premier League victory over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], finishing off a move he had started on the edge of his own [[penalty area]] by smashing the ball into the net, to help Chelsea clinch the title for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{Cite news | url= http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/29307 | archive-url= https://archive.today/20140415165849/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/29307 | url-status= dead | archive-date= 15 April 2014 | title= Chelsea 3 v 0 Man Utd – Match Report | date= 29 April 2006 | access-date= 15 April 2014 | publisher= [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref>

In the [[2006–07 Chelsea F.C. season|2006–07 season]], Carvalho scored again against Manchester United an important goal in a 1–1 draw – a header from a [[Frank Lampard]] corner that also bounced off [[Louis Saha]]'s head.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525070519/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/33560 Man Utd 1 v 1 Chelsea – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> On 7 April, he scored another goal against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], firing a low, 30-yard drive past the reach of Spurs goalkeeper [[Paul Robinson (footballer, born 1979)|Paul Robinson]]; as a result Chelsea narrowed the gap on Premier League leaders Manchester United to three points.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6513349.stm | title = Chelsea 1–0 Tottenham  | date = 7 April 2007 | access-date =11 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] | first=Saj | last=Chowdhury}}</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140415165851/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/34006|title=Chelsea 1 v 0 Tottenham – Match Report}}, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> Just 21 days later, on 28 April, Carvalho injured the medial ligaments of his right leg in a Premier League match against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6578777.stm|publisher= [[BBC Sport]]  | title=Chelsea 2–2 Bolton|date= 28 April 2007 | access-date=9 May 2007 | first=Owen | last=Phillips}}</ref> The injury meant Carvalho missed the second leg of the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] semi-final against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/6604627.stm|publisher= [[BBC Sport]] | title=Chelsea hit by double injury blow | date= 28 April 2007 |access-date=9 May 2007}}</ref> He also missed the [[2007 FA Cup Final|FA Cup final]] against Manchester United, which Chelsea won after a goal from [[Didier Drogba]] during extra time.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525164746/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/36665 Man Utd 0 v 1 Chelsea – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 19 October 2009.</ref> On 18 May 2007, the day of his 29th birthday, Carvalho signed a five-year contract extension with Chelsea, keeping him at the club through the [[2011–12 Chelsea F.C. season|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{Cite news| url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1027456| archive-url=https://archive.today/20140415165932/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1027456| url-status=dead| archive-date=15 April 2014| publisher=[[Chelsea F.C.]]| title=CARVALHO COMMITS FOR FIVE MORE YEARS| date=18 May 2007| access-date=15 April 2014}}</ref> For his great performances during the 2006–07 season, Carvalho has been recognized by a number of organisations. [[Sky Sports]] listed him as one of seven candidates for the Premiership's "Defender of the Year".<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=469156&CPID=8&clid=&lid=1490&title=Defender+of+the+Year&tydna=1 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070704213555/http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=469156&CPID=8&clid=&lid=1490&title=Defender+of+the+Year&tydna=1 | archive-date=4 July 2007 | publisher= [[Sky Sports]] | title=Sky Sports Defender of the Year | date= 29 May 2007 | access-date=4 June 2007}}</ref> He was also one of three Chelsea players nominated for the club's "Player of the Year" honour, which was ultimately won by [[Michael Essien]].<ref>{{Cite news | url= http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1025826 | publisher= [[Chelsea F.C.]] | title= Night of Surprises for Player of the Year | date= 22 May 2007 | access-date= 15 April 2014 | url-status= dead | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130910105334/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1025826 | archive-date= 10 September 2013 | df= dmy-all }}</ref>

[[File:Ricardo Carvalho.JPG|thumb|upright|170px|left|Ricardo Carvalho in a [[Premier League]] game against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on 28 December 2009.]]
Carvalho continued his excellent form into the [[2007–08 Chelsea F.C. season|2007–08 season]]. Following the departure of manager [[José Mourinho]],<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/7003912.stm | title = Mourinho makes shock Chelsea exit | date = 20 September 2007 | access-date =19 October 2009 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> the Spanish champions, Real Madrid, have once again expressed their interest in Carvalho. A Madrid source said, "We have never been able to get Carvalho because of his connection with Mourinho. Now he has left Chelsea, we feel there's a real chance."<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2298274/Real-Madrid-target-Chelseas-Ricardo-Carvalho.html | title = Real Madrid target Chelsea's Ricardo Carvalho | date = 24 April 2008 | access-date =24 November 2009 | work = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | location=London}}</ref> But the Portuguese did not leave the English club. On 26 December 2007, in a 4–4 home draw against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], on the 79th minute, the home side were outmanoeuvred in the middle of the field leaving only goalkeeper [[Petr Čech]] and Carvalho between Villa's [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]], [[Gabriel Agbonlahor]], and the goal, Carvalho attempted the block, went in two-footed and was red carded for the foul,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525165538/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/38740 Chelsea 4 v 4 Aston Villa – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.]] Retrieved 13 January 2010.</ref> in the same night, he issued a public apology for his horror tackle on the forward.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7160652.stm|title = Carvalho sorry for red card lunge|date = 27 December 2007}}</ref> In that season, Carvalho was one of the most consistent performers at the club and his efforts were rewarded when he scored his first goal of the season in his 150th appearance for the club, a 1–0 Premier League victory over [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7316235.stm | title = Chelsea 1–0 Middlesbrough | date = 30 March 2008 | access-date =12 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] | first=Russell | last=Barder}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525165535/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/38393 Chelsea 1 v 0 Middlesbrough – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.]] Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> Later, on 26 April, Carvalho made his 100th appearance in the Premier League against Manchester United, despite Chelsea's 2–1 win, he marred his centenary mark with an error that allowed [[Wayne Rooney]] to equalise.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525113946/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/37357 Chelsea 2 v 1 Man Utd – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.]] Retrieved 19 October 2009.</ref> His solid performances in the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] helped the club reach the [[2008 UEFA Champions League Final|final]], Chelsea's first ever Champions League final appearance and Carvalho's second. ''The Blues'', however, lost 6–5 on [[penalty shootout (football)|penalties]] against Manchester United after a 1–1 draw following [[Extra time (association football)|extra time]]. Carvalho played in all 120 minutes and he was booked one time for a high challenge on [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] right before the end of first half.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180525083917/https://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/43443 Man Utd 1 v 1 Chelsea – Match Report], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> On 8 May 2008, Carvalho was voted by his fellow Chelsea colleagues as Chelsea's "Players Player of the Year", while finishing in the top three for Chelsea's "Player of the Year" award voted by Chelsea fans, along with [[Michael Ballack]] and [[Joe Cole]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1308742 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20140415165812/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1308742 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 15 April 2014 | title = Joe is Fans' Number One | date = 8 May 2008 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | publisher = [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref>

Carvalho opened his account for the [[2008–09 Chelsea F.C. season|2008–09 season]] against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in a 1–3 away victory, on 13 September 2008.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140415165808/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/43844|title=Manchester City 1 v 3 Chelsea – Match Report}}, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> He was a somewhat peripheral figure for the rest of the season, as injury, the sacking of [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]], and subsequent appointment of [[Guus Hiddink]] meant that he lost his place in the team to Brazilian teammate [[Alex (footballer, born June 1982)|Alex]].<ref>{{Cite news| url = http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/premier_league/chelsea/article4805690.ece | title = Ricardo Carvalho knee injury blow to Chelsea | date = 23 September 2008 | access-date =19 October 2009 | work = [[The Times]] | location=London | first=Matt | last=Hughes}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He clocked up only 18 appearances in all competitions, two as substitute, scoring one goal.<ref name="Chelsea FC profile">[http://origin-www.chelseafc.com/page/PlayerProfileDetail/0,,10268~28118,00.html Carvalho's Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140416193254/http://origin-www.chelseafc.com/page/PlayerProfileDetail/0,,10268~28118,00.html |date=16 April 2014 }}, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref>

In July 2009, Carvalho told Chelsea he wanted to quit the club to join [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]]. He said, "I have had four extraordinary years at Chelsea until this year, which has not been very good - indeed it was the worst of my career."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8081914.stm|title = Carvalho ready to leave Chelsea|date = 3 June 2009}}</ref> He played only 18 times in that season at Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/carvalho-eyes-chelsea-exit-1734874.html|title=Carvalho eyes Chelsea exit|website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date=23 October 2011}}</ref> But a move to Inter to link up with Mourinho collapsed when the Italian club wanted to sign him as a free transfer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/chelsea/5712417/Ricardo-Carvalho-and-Deco-furious-as-move-from-Chelsea-to-Inter-Milan-stalls.html|title = Ricardo Carvalho and Deco furious as move from Chelsea to Inter Milan stalls| date=July 2009 }}</ref>

The appointment of [[Carlo Ancelotti]], coupled with recovery from injury, saw Carvalho regain his place in the Chelsea team. He made a fine start to the [[2009–10 Chelsea F.C. season|2009–10 season]], scoring a diving header in the [[2009 FA Community Shield]] match against Manchester United, a game in which he also received the [[Man of the Match]] award. Chelsea got off to a terrible start conceding inside 10 minutes, but second-half goals from Carvalho and Frank Lampard looked enough to pull the team back from behind to win the trophy, only for Wayne Rooney to clip home an equaliser in stoppage time, forcing penalties. Chelsea went on to win the match 4–1 on penalties, following a 2–2 draw at the end of normal time.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140415165825/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/50566|title=Chelsea 2 v 2 Man Utd – Match Report}}, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Retrieved 15 April 2014.</ref> On 20 December 2009, Carvalho made his 200th appearance<ref>{{Cite news | url= http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1909045 | archive-url= https://archive.today/20140415165952/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1909045 | url-status= dead | archive-date= 15 April 2014 | title= CARVALHO: 200 AND COUNTING... | date= 18 December 2009 | access-date= 15 April 2014 | publisher= [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref> in a 1–1 draw against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in the Premier League, where the defender was booked just before the half-hour mark for a challenge on [[Guillermo Franco]], before West Ham had their best chance of the opening stages.<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/48648 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20140415165824/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/48648 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 15 April 2014 | title = West Ham Utd 1 v 1 Chelsea | date = 20 December 2009 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | publisher = [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref> On 24 March, in a 5–0 win over [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]],<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/47453 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20140415165811/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/47453 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 15 April 2014 | title = Portsmouth 0 v 5 Chelsea – Match Report | date = 24 March 2010 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | publisher = [[Chelsea F.C.]] }}</ref> Carvalho suffered ankle ligament damage; it seemed serious but it was not necessary a corrective surgery on this injury, leaving the team with just two first-choice central defenders in Alex and captain John Terry,<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8587952.stm | title = Chelsea rocked by Ricardo Carvalho ankle injury | date = 25 March 2010 | access-date =9 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> and scaring the [[Portugal national football team|Portugal national team]] head coach, [[Carlos Queiroz]], with the risk of not being able to go to [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.publico.pt/noticia/ricardo-carvalho-evita-cirurgia-e-estara-no-mundial-2010-1429638 | title = Futebol: Mundial2010 – Ricardo Carvalho evita cirurgia e estará apto para a seleção | date = 26 March 2010 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | work = [[Diário de Notícias]] | language = pt | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140417095656/http://www.publico.pt/noticia/ricardo-carvalho-evita-cirurgia-e-estara-no-mundial-2010-1429638 | archive-date = 17 April 2014 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Due to the injury, Carvalho missed all the following league matches, including the title match victory against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://origin-www.premierleague.com/page/MatchReports/0,,12306~47531,00.html | title = Match Reports – Chelsea 8 Wigan Athletic 0 | date = 9 May 2010 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | publisher = [[Premier League]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140416175255/http://origin-www.premierleague.com/page/MatchReports/0,,12306~47531,00.html | archive-date = 16 April 2014 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> It was Carvalho's third Premier League title with the Blues. Six days later, on 15 May, he missed another important match, the [[2010 FA Cup Final|2010 FA Cup final]], which they won after a single goal from Didier Drogba. By winning the title, Chelsea secured the first ever [[Double (association football)|Double]] in the club's history.<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/51440 | title = Portsmouth 0 v 1 Chelsea – Match Report | date = 15 May 2010 | access-date = 15 April 2014 | publisher = [[Chelsea F.C.]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140605231016/http://www.chelseafc.com/matchday-live/match/51440 | archive-date = 5 June 2014 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> At the end of the season, on 24 July, ''[[The Sun (United Kingdom)|The Sun]]'' carried reports that Carvalho had expressed his desire to leave Chelsea and link up with former manager José Mourinho, who was now in charge at Real Madrid in Spain.

===Real Madrid (2010–2013)===
[[File:Pato and Carvalho.jpg|thumb|300px|Carvalho and [[Alexandre Pato]] of [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] in a Champions League match in October 2010]]
On 10 August 2010, Real Madrid signed Carvalho for a reported fee of €7.9 (£6.7) million on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8902830.stm | title = Ricardo Carvalho seals move from Chelsea to Real Madrid  | date = 12 August 2010 | access-date =12 September 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> He made his debut on 13 August 2010 in a friendly match against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], which Real Madrid won 4–2 on penalties after a 0–0 draw.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=814211&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120718002605/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=814211&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 18 July 2012 | title = Casillas heroics help Real beat Bayern | date = 14 August 2010 | access-date =24 October 2010 | work = [[ESPNsoccernet]] }}</ref> His [[2010–11 La Liga|La Liga]] debut came on 29 August, in a 0–0 draw against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]],<ref>[http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/302066/report.html Report: Mallorca v Real Madrid – Spanish Primera División – ESPN Soccernet] ESPN, 30 August 2010.</ref> and, in the following match, against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], he scored his first Liga goal; [[Mesut Özil]] raced to the penalty area and managed to thread a low cross for [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], whose first time shot was blocked by the Osasuna's goalkeeper [[Ricardo (footballer, born 1971)|Ricardo]], but the Portuguese managed to tip-toe the rebound for Carvalho to score the go-ahead goal, giving his team a 1–0 home victory.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/48593/real-madrid-vs-osasuna/report | title = Ricardo Carvalho goal gives Jose Mourinho's side first win of the season | date = 11 September 2010 | access-date =12 September 2010 | publisher = Goal.com }}</ref> On 19 October 2010, in a [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group G|UEFA Champions League]] victory against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], Carvalho was named the Man of the match by the Spanish newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.marca.com/2010/10/19/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1287521963.html | title= ¿Carvalho, el fichaje del año? |trans-title= Carvalho, the signing of the year? |work= [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] | language= es | date= 19 October 2010 | access-date=24 October 2010 }}</ref> Some weeks later, on 7 November, Carvalho proved again to be in good shape in a 2–0 [[Madrid Derby|derby]] victory against [[Atlético Madrid]], where he scored his second goal in La Liga, being named again the man of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.marca.com/2010/11/08/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1289201219.html | title= Carvalho impone su ley en las dos áreas del derbi |trans-title= Carvalho imposes his law in the two areas of Derby |work= [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] | language= es | date= 8 November 2010 | access-date=8 November 2010 }}</ref> Next month on day 19, in a 1–0 home victory against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], Carvalho received his first red card for the club; having already been booked in the first half, he was shown a second yellow following an aerial challenge with Sevilla's [[Álvaro Negredo]] in the second half.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/302041/report.html | title = Di Maria lifts scrappy Real | date = 19 December 2010 | access-date =15 April 2014 | work = [[ESPNsoccernet]] }}</ref> On 19 February 2011, he scored his third and last season goal against [[Levante UD|Levante]] in another 2–0 league victory.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/301941/report.html | title = Easy win sees Real close the gap | date = 19 February 2011 | access-date =15 April 2014 | work = [[ESPNsoccernet]] }}</ref> Carvalho made 48 appearances in all competitions that season, bringing calmness and solidness to the defence, and was a heavy reason why Real Madrid had the best defense in Champions League, only letting five goals get past their goalkeeper.

Carvalho started the [[2011–12 Real Madrid C.F. season|2011–12 season]] well and remained as first-choice centre-back along with [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]], until a lower back injury kept him sidelined. He returned to action on 18 January in Real Madrid's 2–1 home defeat to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], in the [[Copa del Rey]] quarter-finals first leg at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].

There was significant speculation about his future with Real Madrid in the [[2012–13 Real Madrid C.F. season|2012–13 season]], with manager José Mourinho publicly stating on 29 August 2012 that "his services were no longer needed" by the club. However, he opted to stay at the club until the end of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2012/08/29/3338327/mourinho-carvalhos-career-is-over-if-he-stays-at-real-madrid | title = Mourinho: Carvalho's career is over if he stays at Real Madrid | date = 29 August 2012 | access-date = 1 October 2012 | publisher = Goal.com | first = Stefan | last = Coerts}}</ref><ref name="Carvalho joins Monaco influx">{{Cite web | url = http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/209470.html | title = Carvalho joins Monaco influx | date = 28 May 2013 | access-date = 1 June 2013 | work = ESPN.co.uk | archive-date = 3 February 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150203005543/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/209470.html | url-status = dead }}</ref>

===Monaco (2013–2016)===
[[File:Ricardo-Carvalho-2015-07.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Carvalho playing for [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] 2015]]
On 28 May 2013, [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] confirmed on their website that they had secured the services of the Portuguese defender from Real Madrid. He moved to the newly promoted [[Ligue 1]] club on a free transfer when his Real Madrid contract expired on 1 July. Carvalho signed a one-year contract with Monaco, with the option of a second year.<ref name="Carvalho joins Monaco influx"/>

Carvalho was sent off for two yellow cards on 10 August 2014, as Monaco began their season with a 2&ndash;1 defeat at home against [[FC Lorient|Lorient]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Monaco 1-2 Lorient|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28687991|access-date=2 September 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|date=10 August 2014}}</ref> On 14 April 2015, he fouled [[Álvaro Morata]] to concede a penalty which was converted by [[Arturo Vidal]] as Monaco lost to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the first leg of the quarter-finals of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Juventus 1-0 Monaco|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32289613|access-date=14 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 April 2015}}</ref> In July 2015, he signed a new one-year deal, keeping him at the club until July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/AS_Monaco/status/616726949231259649|title=AS MONACO 🇲🇨 on Twitter}}</ref>

On 10 August 2016, it was announced that Monaco had not renewed his contract, ending a three-year spell with the [[Ligue 1]] club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11816/10530511/monaco-release-former-chelsea-defender-ricardo-carvalho|title=Monaco release former Chelsea defender Ricardo Carvalho|website=skysports.com|access-date=23 March 2018}}</ref>

=== Shanghai SIPG (2017–2018) ===
On 9 January 2017, Carvalho was announcing his engagement by [[André Villas-Boas]]'s [[Shanghai SIPG]] in the [[Chinese Super League]]. He officially joined Shanghai SIPG on 15 February 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2017-02-15/doc-ifyarmcu6011051.shtml | title= 上港官方宣布卡瓦略加盟 最后一块外援拼图落定 |publisher= Sina | language= zh | date= 15 February 2017 | access-date=15 February 2017 }}</ref>
On 6 October 2017, Carvalho was handed a seven-month suspended prison sentence in Spain for tax fraud.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/11069613/ricardo-carvalho-given-prison-sentence-for-tax-fraud-in-spain|title=Ricardo Carvalho given prison sentence for tax fraud in Spain|website=skysports.com|access-date=23 March 2018}}</ref>

==International career==

===Senior team===
[[File:Portugal 2-3 Denmark.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Left to right: [[Paulo Ferreira]], [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]], Ricardo Carvalho and [[José Bosingwa]], during a [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification]] match against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], on 10 September 2008.]]
During the 2003–04 season, Carvalho earned his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for the [[Portugal national football team|Portugal national team]] on 11 October 2003 in a 5–3 friendly match win over [[Albania national football team|Albania]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=175810 |title= Scolari: "Meia-distância pode ser arma para o futuro" |trans-title= Scolari: "half-distance can be a weapon for the future" |publisher= [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]] |language= pt |date= 12 October 2003 |access-date= 11 January 2011 |archive-date= 6 April 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120406191439/http://www.record.xl.pt/arquivo/interior.aspx?content_id=175810 |url-status= dead }}</ref> He established himself as a key member of the national team starting XI during the [[UEFA Euro 2004]] championship on home soil, after replacing captain [[Fernando Couto]] in the heart of Portugal's defence following the team's defeat against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] in the opening group game.<ref name="Chelsea_land_Carvalho">{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/3928771.stm | title = Chelsea land Carvalho | date = 28 July 2004 | access-date =24 November 2009 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> In the tournament, he was nominated for the [[UEFA Euro 2004#Awards|UEFA Euro Team of the Tournament]] along with his compatriots [[Maniche]], [[Luís Figo]] and Cristiano Ronaldo.<ref name="Euro 2004 team of the tournament">{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/greece/3866823.stm | title = Zagorakis named top player  | date = 5 July 2004 | access-date =11 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref> Carvalho formed a strong partnership with Jorge Andrade in the Portuguese defence as his country reached the [[UEFA Euro 2004 Final|final]], though they lost 1–0 to Greece in a stunning upset.<ref name="report">{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Szreter |title=Greece kings of Europe |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1623/match=1059194/postmatch/report/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111130174331/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1623/match=1059194/postmatch/report/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 November 2011 |work=Union of European Football Associations |date=4 July 2004 |access-date=24 May 2008}}</ref> Carvalho started in all of Portugal's six games in the tournament, including an epic game against [[England national football team|England]], where the defender was named [[Carlsberg Group|Carlsberg]] Man of the Match,<ref>{{Cite web | url = http://www.farsons.com/page.asp?n=newsdetails&i=2468 | title = Carlsberg Man of the Match Award presented by Maltese fan | date = 28 June 2004 | access-date = 4 October 2010 | work = [[Simonds Farsons Cisk|Farsons]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110710225627/http://www.farsons.com/page.asp?n=newsdetails&i=2468 | archive-date = 10 July 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> and Portugal emerged victorious [[UEFA Euro 2004 knockout stage#Quarter-finals|6–5]] on penalties.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3830451.stm Portugal break England hearts] BBC Sport, 24 June 2004</ref> [[BBC Sport]] football expert [[Alan Hansen]] said that Carvalho was, along with [[Sol Campbell]], the best defender at Euro 2004.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3535816.stm | title = Alan Hansen's title verdict | date = 9 August 2004 | access-date =11 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref>

Carvalho represented Portugal at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] in Germany, finishing fourth overall. During the quarter-final game against England, referee [[Horacio Elizondo]] adjudged [[Wayne Rooney]] to have trodden on Carvalho's groin, right in front of him, and the English player was sent off for violent conduct.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991618.stm | title = England 0–0 Portugal | date = 1 July 2006 | access-date =12 April 2010 | publisher = BBC Sport }}</ref> The English media, however, speculated that teammate Cristiano Ronaldo had influenced Elizondo's decision by aggressively complaining, after which he was seen in replays winking at the Portuguese bench following Rooney’s dismissal.<ref>{{Cite web| url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=373109&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120526061724/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=373109&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 26 May 2012 | title = Ronaldo: I never asked for Rooney red card | date = 2 July 2006 | access-date =10 April 2010 | work = [[ESPNsoccernet]] }}</ref> In the following semi-final game against [[France national football team|France]] in [[Munich]] on 5 July 2006, Carvalho was whistled for a foul against France's [[Thierry Henry]] in the penalty area, resulting in a penalty kick. [[Zinedine Zidane]] converted the spot kick to give France a 1–0 win over Portugal.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991632.stm | title = Portugal 0–1 France  | date = 5 July 2006 | access-date =12 April 2010 | publisher = BBC Sport }}</ref> Also in the same game, Carvalho was booked with his second yellow card of the knockout phase, and was forced to miss the third place game against hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]] on 8 July in [[Stuttgart]], which ended in a 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991644.stm | title = Germany 3–1 Portugal  | date = 8 July 2006 | access-date =12 April 2010 | publisher = BBC Sport }}</ref> He in played each of his team's other preceding matches throughout the World Cup, as a member of Portugal's central defensive pairing in the team's starting lineup alongside [[Fernando Meira]], and as a result of his performances, he was one of the 23 players nominated for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup#All-star team|All Star Team of the tournament]].<ref name="2006 FIFA World Cup All Star Team">{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/news/newsid=31923.html |title=''Azzurri'' prominent in All Star Team |publisher=FIFA |date=7 July 2006 |access-date=24 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100614214225/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/news/newsid%3D31923.html |archive-date=14 June 2010 |url-status=dead  }}</ref><ref name="2006 World Cup All-Star Squad">{{cite news |url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/france-italy-dominate-world-cup-all-star-squad-1.572395 |title=France, Italy dominate World Cup all-star squad |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |agency=Associated Press |date=7 July 2006 |access-date=11 August 2006 }}</ref>

Carvalho was named in the [[UEFA Euro 2008 squads#Group A|Portuguese squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]]. He played in three of Portugal's four matches in the tournament, including the 2–0 win against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] and the 3–1 victory over [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2008 Group A|group stage]] and the [[UEFA Euro 2008 knockout stage#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] match where Portugal lost 3–2 to Germany. Two years later, Carvalho was named again in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup squads#Portugal|Portuguese squad]] for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]]. He formed a partnership with [[Bruno Alves]] in the centre of defence, playing in all group stage matches without conceding a goal. This time, Portugal reached the round of 16, where they subsequently lost 1–0 against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] via a [[David Villa]] goal.<ref name="espport">{{cite web |title = Spain 1 – 0 Portugal – Villa nets winner for Spain | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=264114&league=FIFA.WORLD&cc=5739&ver=global | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130103111936/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=264114&league=FIFA.WORLD&cc=5739&ver=global | url-status = dead | archive-date = 3 January 2013 | publisher = ESPN | date = 29 June 2010 | access-date = 29 June 2010}}</ref>

On 31 August 2011, Carvalho retired from international football after leaving the concentration without talking to his coach and teammates before Portugal's match against [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus]] for a [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying|Euro 2012 qualifying]] match, announcing in a statement carried by state news agency Lusa he had been "disrespected".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-euro-portugal-idUKTRE77U4YC20110831|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808031854/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-euro-portugal-idUKTRE77U4YC20110831|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 August 2016|title=Ronaldo warns against Portugal slipup|newspaper=Reuters|date=31 August 2011}}</ref>

On 3 October 2014, after an absence of more than three years, Carvalho was called up by newly appointed Portugal manager [[Fernando Santos (football coach)|Fernando Santos]], for the friendly against France and the [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying Group I|Euro 2016 qualifying]] match against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hanson|first1=Peter|title=Ronaldo returns for Portugal|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/91/portugal/2014/10/03/5154177/ronaldo-returns-for-portugal|access-date=7 October 2014|work=Goal.com|date=3 October 2014}}</ref> On 29 March 2015, in a qualifier against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]], he headed the opening goal in a 2&ndash;1 home victory, his first international goal for over eight years.<ref>{{cite news|title=Portugal see off Serbia to top Group I|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d7ff0cbb8bf-7677474ee0fd-1000--portugal-see-off-serbia-to-top-group-i/|access-date=29 March 2015|publisher=UEFA|date=29 March 2015}}</ref> At 38, he was the oldest outfield player at the [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]] finals in France.<ref>{{cite news|title=Euro 2016: A final swansong for Ricardo Carvalho?|url=http://www.sportskeeda.com/football/euro-2016-final-swansong-ricardo-carvalho|access-date=6 June 2016|publisher=Sportskeeda|date=4 June 2016}}</ref> He started in all three of his team's group stages matches, but was dropped from the starting line-up for the knock-out stages of the competition;<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2651593-ranking-portugals-players-on-their-euro-2016-performances |title=Ranking Portugal's Players on Their Euro 2016 Performances |publisher=Bleacher Report |last1=Jones |first1=Mark |date=12 July 2016 |access-date=1 May 2020 }}</ref> Portugal went on to win the tournament, defeating the hosts 1–0 in the [[UEFA Euro 2016 Final|final]] in extra time, although Carvalho remained on the bench.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36696772 |title=Portugal 1 France 0 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 July 2016 |access-date=11 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710233341/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36696772 |archive-date=10 July 2016 |url-status=live |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:Ibra and Carvalho.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Carvalho (right) defending against [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] (left).]]
Carvalho was always a [[centre back]] who stood out in particular for his intelligence, and ability to read the game and time his challenges. He was quick, good in the air and possessed superb technique and good passing ability, which led him to be compared to the legendary Italian defender [[Franco Baresi]].<ref>{{Cite news| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3760085.stm | title = Who's coming to England? | date = 29 May 2004 | access-date =12 April 2010 | publisher = [[BBC Sport]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/ricardo-carvalho-the-toughest-line-of-defence-1.935750|title=Ricardo Carvalho: The toughest line of defence|publisher=CBC Sports|author1=Matthew Scianitti|date=3 June 2010|access-date=8 July 2016}}</ref><ref name="blindspot">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/jan/19/nemanja-vidic-footballer-of-year|title=Judges have a blindspot when destroyers like Vidic play a blinder|work=The Guardian|last1=Bagchi|first1=Rob|date=19 January 2011|access-date=2 February 2017}}</ref> Although he did not possess the physical strength of other defenders, he was known for his tenacity and hard-tackling style of play; in an interview with the Champions League's official magazine, Carvalho said of his playing style and physique:
{{blockquote|(...) Players who grow in England are different, they are tough, strong. My first year was difficult because I wanted the ball, wanted to play, and the pace here is unbelievable. The players are physically strong, and if they don't play well they kick. It wasn't my game. And every time I jumped with my arm my shoulder would pop out. With time it got weaker. In May 2005 I had an operation, I started to work a bit in the gym, which I'd never done before, and I improved a lot. (...) My body is not as strong as a normal centre-back in England, but I like to play hard and tackle. I love to make crazy tackles, I like to slide on the ground.<ref name="CL_interview">{{Cite web| url = http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1446875.html#carvalho+learns+hard | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100212051625/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=1446875.html#carvalho+learns+hard | url-status = dead | archive-date = 12 February 2010 | title = Carvalho strengthens Chelsea's grip at the top | date = 9 February 2010 | access-date = 12 April 2010 | publisher = [[UEFA]] }}</ref>
}} As such throughout his career, he was often paired with a more physical centre-back, such as his defensive partner at Chelsea, [[John Terry]], whose powerful and aggressive playing style was complemented by Carvalho's mobility, technique, intelligence, speed of thought, and ball–playing ability.<ref name="blindspot"/><ref name="Terry is the Premier League's best central defender">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/blog/name/67/post/2271191/headline |title=John Terry is the Premier League's best central defender this season |publisher=ESPN FC |last1=Cox |first1=Michael |date=30 January 2015 |access-date=27 April 2020 }}</ref><ref name="lack of form">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/3023433/John-Terrys-lack-of-form-being-hidden-behind-Ricardo-Carvalhos-brilliance-Football.html |title=John Terry's lack of form being hidden behind Ricardo Carvalho's brilliance |work=The Telegraph |last1=Robson |first1=Stewart |date=20 September 2008 |access-date=27 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/sports/soccer/news/_/id/7268298/epl-michael-cox-five-ways-fix-chelsea-soccer |title=Five ways to fix Chelsea |publisher=ESPN FC |last1=Cox |first1=Michael |date=22 November 2011 |access-date=27 April 2020 }}</ref><ref name="The special team">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2553961/Jose-Mourinhos-Fantasy-Football-XI-The-special-team-Football.html |title=Jose Mourinho's Fantasy Football XI: The special team |work=The Telegraph |last1=Mourinho |first1=Jose |date=13 August 2008 |access-date=30 April 2020 }}</ref> Despite not being as tall as most centre-backs at 1.83 m (6 ft 0 in), Carvalho was also known for his ability to win aerial duels against larger, more physical opponents, as demonstrated by the three headed goals he scored against Manchester United with [[Rio Ferdinand]] and [[Nemanja Vidić]] in defence. In the same UEFA Champions League's official magazine interview, he stated:

{{blockquote|(...) At Porto there were taller centre-backs than me, but they were on the bench because I was quicker, I turned quicker. I said to the coach, 'I have to grow a bit.' But he said: 'No, you'll start to get slow to turn, slow to run. You're good, you are there now.' (...) A defender is one thing, football is about defending and playing. Normally, play comes from us defenders so we have to defend, not concede, close down space, be focused on the strikers and after all that try to get a move going. (...)<ref name="CL_interview"/>
}}

Carvalho's Real Madrid profile described him as "known for his perfect positioning, his foresight and his ability to advance the ball out of the first third".<ref>{{cite web|title=Player Profile|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041476158/1330011307313/jugador/Jugador/Carvalho.htm|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120903055928/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193041476158/1330011307313/jugador/Jugador/Carvalho.htm|archive-date=3 September 2012|access-date=28 March 2012}}</ref> At his peak, Carvalho was regarded by several pundits and football figures as one of the best defenders in the world,<ref name="The special team"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/oct/19/aston-villa-chelsea-premier-league |title=Martin O'Neill praises impact of defenders as Chelsea are kept at bay |work=The Guardian |last1=McCarra |first1=Kevin |date=19 October 2009 |access-date=30 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/475827-world-football-the-current-best-11-defenders-in-the-world |title=World Football: The Current Best 11 Defenders In The World |publisher=Bleacher Report |last1=Traquete |first1=Manuel |date=28 September 2010 |access-date=30 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://metro.co.uk/2017/05/15/chelsea-have-jose-mourinho-to-thank-for-every-premier-league-title-they-have-won-says-gary-neville-6639649/ |title=Chelsea have Jose Mourinho to thank for every Premier League title they have won, says Gary Neville |work=Metro |last1=Barry |first1=Coral |date=15 May 2017 |access-date=30 April 2020 }}</ref> and is considered to be one of the greatest defenders in the history of the Premier League.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/05/12/the-20-best-premier-league-defenders-ever-where-does-john-terry/ricardo-carvalho/ |title=The 20 best Premier League defenders ever: where does John Terry rank? |work=The Telegraph |date=12 May 2016 |access-date=30 April 2020 }}</ref>

==Coaching career==

Throughout [[André Villas-Boas]]' time as manager of French club [[Olympique de Marseille]], Carvalho served as his assistant manager.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.onzemondial.com/ligue-1/2019-2020/om-le-premier-entrainement-de-ricardo-carvalho-192003 | title= OM: Premier entrainement de Ricardo Carvalho |publisher= [[Onze Mondial]] | language= fr | date= 6 July 2019 | access-date=25 July 2019 }}</ref>

He joined the coaching staff of [[Roberto Martínez]] with the [[Portugal national football team|Portugal national team]] in 2023, serving as Assistant Head Coach to Martínez alongside Scotsman [[Austin MacPhee]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seleção A - A equipa técnica |url=https://www.fpf.pt/pt/Sele%C3%A7%C3%B5es/Futebol-Masculino/Sele%C3%A7%C3%A3o-A/Equipa-t%C3%A9cnica |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=FPF |language=pt-PT}}</ref> During his time with Portugal, the team has won the [[2025 UEFA Nations League Finals|2025 UEFA Nations League]], beating Spain in the [[2025 UEFA Nations League final|final]] on penalties <ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=The official website for European football |url=https://www.uefa.com/errors/ |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref>; additionally, the team qualified for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], finishing second in their group.
